## Summary

I wired up a welcome email that's sent via the background queue after registration, without blocking the request:

- **`config/queue.ts`** / **`config/mail.ts`** — new config modules that build a `QueueManager`/`MailManager` from `QUEUE_CONNECTION` (`sync` dev driver / `redis` production driver) and `MAIL_MAILER` (`log` dev transport / `resend` production transport), reading `MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS`/`MAIL_FROM_NAME` for the sender. Neither existed before; the framework's built-in `QueueServiceProvider`/`MailServiceProvider` construct unconfigured managers and never call the required `setQueueDriver()`/`setMailManager()` globals that `Job.dispatch()` and job-side mail sending depend on.
- **`app/Providers/QueueProvider.ts`** / **`app/Providers/MailProvider.ts`** — new providers, registered in `src/app.ts`, that bind those managers into the container and (critically) call `setQueueDriver()`, `setMailManager()`, and `registerJob()` at boot so dispatch/send actually work.
- **`app/Mail/WelcomeMail.ts`** — a `Mail` mailable whose `build()` sets the subject to `Welcome to <APP_NAME>, <name>!` and a plain-text greeting.
- **`app/Jobs/SendWelcomeEmailJob.ts`** — a `Job` whose `handle()` sends `WelcomeMail` via the global mail manager.
- **`app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.ts`** — after creating the user (and before login/redirect), dispatches `SendWelcomeEmailJob`; validation/duplicate-email failures throw earlier and never reach this line, so nothing is queued on a refused registration.
- **`tests/RegisterController.test.ts`** — new tests using `@guren/testing`'s `fakeQueue()`/`fakeMail()` to verify: exactly one job is queued and nothing is sent immediately after registering; running that job (via `processJob`) sends exactly one correctly-addressed/subjected/bodied email; and a refused registration queues and sends nothing.
